Module–Trait Association — Motor Cortex (Bulk RNA-seq)

Extended Analysis: Age, FTD/AD Comorbidity, Site of Motor Onset

ALS Deconvolution Project

2026-04-28

What this analysis adds: Extends the original Motor Cortex WGCNA module–trait correlation (ALS, Sex, RIN, C9ORF72) with three new trait categories:

  • Age at Death — tests for age-driven transcriptional changes that might confound ALS associations.
  • FTD/AD Comorbidity — binary indicator (1 if Subject.Group.Subcategory contains Frontotemporal Dementia or Alzheimer’s Disease).
  • Site of Motor Onset — three dummy columns:
    • Onset_Limb: all limb/extremity variants, combined entries (e.g., “Bulbar and Limb”), and Generalized.
    • Onset_Bulbar: Bulbar, combined entries, and Generalized.
    • Onset_Axial: Axial, combined entries, and Generalized.

Filter (Section 4): Only modules with ALS p < 0.05 and RIN p > 0.05 are retained — significantly ALS-associated but independent of RNA quality.

Dataset: Motor Cortex — Bulk RNA-seq  |  Retained samples: 320  |  Non-grey modules: 52

5 Summary & Brief Analysis

11 module(s) survived the dual filter: 5 up-regulated and 6 down-regulated in ALS.

  • The Motor Cortex contains samples from lateral and medial sub-regions, which may introduce within-tissue heterogeneity. Modules passing the RIN filter are less likely to reflect tissue-quality differences between sub-regions.
  • Correlation with Site of Motor Onset (Limb vs Bulbar) may reflect differential involvement of primary motor cortex regions in distinct ALS subtypes.
  • FTD/AD comorbidity associations could highlight shared or distinct neurodegeneration pathways between ALS and frontotemporal/Alzheimer’s pathology in the motor cortex.
